title: Lunch break
intro: It is lunch break in the school yard. Your classmate is eating and laughing with friends. Suddenly she starts to cough and holds her throat. Help her.

sources.title: IFRC International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2025

characters.name: Classmate
characters.description: A girl in your class who is choking on a piece of food.

characters.name: Your friend
characters.description: Your classmate, who stays with you and can call 907.

characters.name: Another student
characters.description: A student nearby who wants to help but gives wrong advice.

characters.name: Teacher
characters.description: A teacher who comes over after the food is out.

characters.name: Ambulance crew
characters.description: The ambulance team who take over when they arrive.

facts.text: She can cough and make sounds, so some air is getting in.
She cannot cough, speak or breathe. The food is blocking her airway.
She does not respond and is not breathing normally.

actions.label: Ask: Are you choking?
actions.hint: Ask her straight away. If she nods, she is choking.

actions.label: Tell her: keep coughing
actions.hint: If she can cough, coughing is the best way to clear it. Stay with her and tell her to keep coughing.

actions.label: Give a back blow
actions.hint: Look: can she still cough and make sounds? What works best right now?

actions.label: Give her some water
actions.hint: Can she swallow while her throat is blocked?

actions.label: Put fingers in her mouth
actions.hint: Fingers can push the food further down. Is there a safer way?

actions.label: Run to find a teacher
actions.hint: Should she be left alone while she is choking? Who else could go?

actions.label: Lean her forward
actions.hint: Stand to her side, a little behind. Hold her chest with one hand and lean her well forward, so the food comes out of her mouth.

actions.label: Give a back blow
actions.hint: Hit firmly between her shoulder blades with the heel of your hand. Give up to 5 blows. Stop if the food comes out.

actions.label: Give an abdominal thrust
actions.hint: If 5 back blows do not work: stand behind her, put a fist just above her belly button, hold it with your other hand and pull sharply in and up. Up to 5, then back blows again.

actions.label: Ask a friend to call 907
actions.hint: Do not stop helping her to make the call yourself. Send your friend to call 907 now.

actions.label: Stay with her, calm her
actions.hint: Stay with her. Let her sit and rest. Tell her she is safe now.

actions.label: Get her a health check
actions.hint: Tell a teacher. She should see a health worker: back blows and thrusts can hurt, and a bit of food can stay behind.

actions.label: Start chest compressions
actions.hint: Lay her on her back. Push hard and fast in the centre of her chest, 100 to 120 times a minute. Keep going until help takes over.

actions.label: Wait for her to wake up
actions.hint: She is not responding and not breathing normally. Can waiting help her?

lines.text: She was laughing while she ate. Now she is coughing a lot!
Help! She was eating, and now she is coughing and holding her throat!
(She coughs hard. Her face is red and her eyes are watering.)
(She nods. She holds her throat with both hands.)
(She keeps coughing hard. Air is still getting in.)
(She is still coughing hard. Hitting her back does not help while she can cough.)
Give her some water!
(She cannot swallow. The water makes her splutter and choke more.)
Put your fingers in her mouth and pull it out!
(She gags and pulls away. Fingers can push the food further down.)
(She cannot cough, speak or breathe. She points at her throat.)
(You hold her chest with one hand and lean her well forward.)
(A firm blow between her shoulder blades with the heel of your hand.)
(From behind, fist above her belly button, you pull sharply in and up.)
Okay! I am calling 907 now. Keep helping her!
907 says an ambulance is on the way. Keep helping her!
It is still stuck! She still cannot breathe!
Do not leave her! She cannot breathe. Stay and help her!
(The food flies out. She coughs and takes a big breath.) I... I can breathe.
It came out! You did it!
Thank you for staying with me. My throat hurts a little.
Well done. I will take her to the health centre to be checked. Back blows and thrusts can hurt, and a bit of food can stay behind.
(She goes limp, and you lower her to the floor. She does not respond and is not breathing normally.)
She is not answering! What do we do?
(You push hard and fast on the centre of her chest.)
She is not waking up! She needs help now!
We are the ambulance crew. We will take over now. You did the right thing to push on her chest.

items.teachingPoint: Ask "Are you choking?" If she nods but cannot speak, act at once.

items.description: Told her to keep coughing while she could
items.teachingPoint: If she can cough, tell her to keep coughing. Coughing is the best way to clear it. Stay with her.

items.description: Leaned her forward before the back blows
items.teachingPoint: Lean her well forward first, so the food comes out of her mouth and does not go further down.

items.description: Gave back blows quickly when she could not cough, speak or breathe
items.teachingPoint: If she cannot cough, speak or breathe, give up to 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand, straight away.

items.description: Gave 5 back blows before abdominal thrusts
items.teachingPoint: Back blows first, up to 5. If they do not work, give up to 5 abdominal thrusts. Keep repeating 5 and 5 until the food comes out.
Send a friend to call 907 while you keep helping her. If the food does not come out, or she stops responding, the ambulance is already on the way.

items.description: Started chest compressions within a minute of her collapse
items.teachingPoint: If she stops responding and is not breathing normally, start chest compressions at once and keep going until help takes over.

items.description: Pushed at 100 to 120 a minute for most sets
items.teachingPoint: Push 100 to 120 times a minute. A hands-on class teaches the depth: 5 to 6 cm.

items.description: Stayed with her after the food came out
items.teachingPoint: Stay with her until she is calm and breathing normally.

items.description: Made sure a health worker checks her
items.teachingPoint: After choking, she should be checked by a health worker. Back blows and thrusts can hurt, and a bit of food can stay behind.

harms.description: Hit her back while she could still cough
harms.teachingPoint: While she can cough, coughing works best. Start back blows only when she cannot cough, speak or breathe.
Never give a choking person a drink. She cannot swallow, and it can make the choking worse.
Do not put your fingers in her mouth to search for the food. It can push the food further down.

harms.description: Left her alone to find a teacher
harms.teachingPoint: Do not leave someone who is choking. Stay and help her, and send someone else for help.

harms.description: Waited for her to wake up
harms.teachingPoint: If she stops responding, make sure 907 is called and start chest compressions straight away.

disclaimer: A practice game. It does not replace hands-on first aid training. In an emergency in Addis Ababa, call 907.
